messages:
maria: sec-bot flagged an odd domain-verify flow a few mins ago. admin role was granted after domain verify for org/245 even though user was a normal org member. looks like subdomain ownership can be claimed via a crafted request. @kevin can you take a look?

kevin: on it. i see a burst of /api/orgs/245/domains/verify from 3 IPs. logs show verify -> set_admin flow in the same request. pulling recent deploys and code paths.

sec-bot: ALERT: anomalous_subdomain_claim pattern matched. endpoints: /api/orgs/:id/domains/verify. score: 0.87. sample ip: 18.205.34.12. user-agent: curl/7.86.0.

samir: quick hypothesis — the verify handler uses the domain claim + cookie to set `is_admin` when domain is verified. if an attacker controls subdomain routing or forges host header and we only rely on Host header + cookie, they might escalate. checking ingress and proxy header logic.

jen: if this is true we need to contain immediately. disable auto-admin-grant on verify, fallback to manual approval. also we should inform support for affected orgs.

kevin: reproducer i used locally (sanitized):
```
curl -v -X POST https://app.redwood.test/api/orgs/245/domains/verify \n  -H "Host: evil.example.com" \n  -H "Cookie: session=eyJ..." \n  -d '{"domain":"evil.example.com","token":"owned"}'
```
Response sometimes returns 200 and role change.

maria: ops, can you apply a short-term prod hold? block the verify route or add a 403 if Host header != org-expected-host.

ops-oncall: doing a hotfix, setting an ingress rule to reject Host mismatches and disabling the domain-verify worker. rolling in 30s. posting status in #incidents once live.

kevin: pushing a quick patch: remove auto_admin flag and require signed DNS challenge token validated against KMS-signed nonce. PR: https://github.com/redwood/portal/pull/5234 (WIP). also adding an audit event for domain.verify with previous role and actor.

samir: i'll run an RBAC audit across orgs to find any accounts that unexpectedly have admin grants in the last 7 days. query: `SELECT * FROM role_grants WHERE reason = 'domain.verify' AND created_at > now()-interval '7 days'`. will provide list and owner mapping.

jen: communications plan: escalate to legal if any billing or data access issue, notify affected org owners, and post an internal summary. we should avoid public disclosure until fixes are deployed. i'll draft a short internal blurb.

kevin: logs snippet (redacted):
```
2026-03-20T14:02:11Z INFO domain-verify user=uid:908 org=245 ip=18.205.34.12 host=evil.example.com result=verified set_admin=true
2026-03-20T14:02:12Z INFO role-change user=uid:908 org=245 from=member to=admin by=domain-verify
```

maria: immediate mitigation checklist we agreed: 1) ingress host validation (ops) 2) disable auto-admin-grant (kevin) 3) run RBAC audit and rollback grants if malicious (samir) 4) rotate tokens for affected orgs + revoke sessions (ops) 5) create detection rule for domain-verify role changes (sec) 6) update runbook and add unit/e2e tests that simulate host forging.

ops-oncall: ingress rule live, domain-verify worker paused, queued jobs killed. no customer-facing downtime reported.

kevin: pushed PR that gates admin grant behind a KMS-signed challenge + verifies Host header and Origin. also added an audit log entry with challenge id. linking tests. PR merged to hotfix branch, will promote after security review.

samir: RBAC audit found 3 accounts granted admin via domain.verify in last 72h. two are internal test orgs, one appears customer-facing. i'm exporting affected users now and creating ticket INC-2026-45.

maria: good catch. ops please rotate any API keys or service tokens tied to that org and rotate the org owner session tokens.

ops-oncall: rotating keys for org 245, revoking all active sessions, and creating a change log entry. estimated complete in 15m.

jen: comms: initial internal note drafted. waiting for kevin & samir confirmation before notifying customer. holding public disclosure.

kevin: small KMS question — we should use envelope encryption with HMAC of the challenge to avoid replay. can the KMS team confirm signing TTL and rotate policy? tagging here for follow-up.

samir: follow-ups and long-term actions: - add host binding and signed DNS challenge enforced in code - add mandatory audit entries for any role change - add detection rule in sec-sensor for `role-change` where source=domain-verify - update the runbook with exact revocation steps - consider integrating automated KMS verification helper lib for teams.

maria: owners: kevin=code fix + tests, samir=rbac audit + detection rule, jen=customer/legal comms, ops-oncall=rotate/revoke + ingress. i'll create a post-incident summary doc and schedule a 30m blameless postmortem tomorrow.

sec-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-45 created and linked to this thread. severity: high. added to #incidents, pager duty notified.

jen: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source of truth. i'll add the draft internal note and the timeline to the incident ticket.

maria: closing loop for this thread for now. we'll reconvene after postmortem. :thumbsup:
